# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Verified by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymPlayer` consumes the shared input mapping (calls `_readPlayerInput` or an extracted shared input helper) and no longer inlines the `fourDirHandler`/`asteroidsHandler` branch. Verified by a source guard and by `GymPlayer.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3** — Timed-weapon expiry, P5 multipliers and auto-fire ordering are identical in the game and every gym for the same input and `dt`. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test booting `PlayScene` and a gym, applying a P5 effect and asserting the same speed/fire-rate outcome.
- [ ] **AC4** — `GymPowerUpsCombat` no longer uses a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the player path; the player is advanced from the supplied `dt` (the enemy-clock fix is child #2).
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing scene suites pass unchanged; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard covers `_tickPlayer`.
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4.
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — new shared `_tickPlayer(dt)`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — consume the shared step.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ8 (from epic):** should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper.*

## Plan — changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0`: autoplan pre-check returned `decision: skip` (placeholder effort Extra Small / risk Low). Planning auto-completed via the six automated review stages. No child items were created: the parent epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` already decomposed register gaps 1 & 11 into this leaf task, and its ACs contain the test/verification obligations. No blocking clarifications were required; clarifications and one flagged AC wording issue are recorded below.

## Plan — automated review summary

Retained as a leaf task for direct implementation (measurable ACs + minimal implementation sketch):

- **Requirements & AC alignment:** AC1–AC7 trace to epic gaps 1 (player-control step duplicated) and 11 (`GymPlayer` not on the shared control core). AC1 names four consumers; AC2 covers `GymPlayer`; AC4 covers `GymPowerUpsCombat`; together they cover every consumer named in the summary. OQ8 is answered by AC2.
- **Completeness:** `## Acceptance Criteria` is present and the `## Key Files` paths are syntactically valid; all 11 referenced files exist at HEAD (`7bfe98f`).
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children. This item is the prerequisite (epic child #1) for boss integration (child #6) and the parity guard (child #10). Tests are embedded in AC1–AC5, so the test-first intent is satisfied without separate children.
- **Scope sizing:** one focused refactor (add `_tickPlayer`, migrate six scenes, tests, docs) — a deliverable increment.
- **Acceptance & testability:** all ACs are pass/fail; AC3 (cross-scene equivalence) and AC5 (duplicate-body guard) name automated verification.
- **Polish & handoff:** description is actionable; the Key Files list matches the consumer set.
- **AC coverage review:** `run_coverage_review` returned `recommendation: proceed` (leaf item; no children).

## Plan — clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: "OQ8 — should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal?" Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Research (HEAD `7bfe98f`; read of `PlayScene.tick` L557–572, `GymFormationScene.tick` L1299–1318, `GymWeapons.tick` L178–195, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` L154–170, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick` L258–275): the scenes run **subsets with different ordering**, not identical copies — `PlayScene` runs tickWeaponTimers → multipliers → `_handleTeleport` → input → physics → auto-fire; `GymFormationScene` runs timers → multipliers → input → physics → auto-fire with teleport later; `GymWeapons` omits the P5 multipliers; `GymPowerUpsUtility` omits tickWeaponTimers and auto-fire; `GymPowerUpsCombat` omits timers, multipliers and auto-fire. Resolution (epic assumption, "the shipped game is canonical"): the shared `_tickPlayer(dt)` runs the full ordered sequence and each gym's absent feature resolves to a no-op (multiplier 1, empty weapon list). Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" Research: the only fixed 16 ms step is `_nextFireTime += 16` inside `_tickScouts` (`GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` L424), which is the **enemy-fire** clock and belongs to epic child #2 (`AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46`, "Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock"); the player path already advances from the supplied `dt`. **OPEN QUESTION (AC4 wording):** AC4 should be read as "the `GymPowerUpsCombat` player path uses the supplied `dt`" (already true); the 16 ms enemy clock is fixed by child #2, not by this item. Intent is clear enough to implement; the wording is flagged for correction rather than rewritten here (rewriting could change intent).

**OQ-NOTE (effort/risk):** the autoplan pre-check generated a zeroed placeholder estimate (O=M=P=0, 0.00 h → Extra Small / Low) because `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` submits a fixed `{o:0,m:0,p:0}` payload. Treat the `effort`/`risk` fields as a placeholder; `<WIP-id>` should receive a genuine `/skill:effort-and-risk` estimate before implementation is dispatched.

# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.

## Problem statement

The automated gameplay capture path (`npm run capture`) produces a **silent**
WebM clip: audio was explicitly deferred when the spike
(AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) shipped. The result is a demo/attract clip that must be
manually paired with audio before it is usable. This item adds game audio to
the captured clip so a single command yields a self-contained demo video.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture` to produce a
gameplay video that contains the game audio, so demo/attract clips are usable
without a separate manual audio pass.

**Outcome:** a single documented command writes a WebM whose audio track
contains the game's SFX (synchronised with the captured gameplay), with the
audio's presence verified by the capture probe and recorded in the capture
report — while the capture path stays opt-in and leaves `npm test` /
`npm run build` unchanged.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Generates demo, attract and
  marketing clips. Wants one command that yields a clip with sound so no
  second audio pass is needed.
  - *As the maintainer, I run `npm run capture` and get a WebM with the game
    audio already in it, so I can publish it directly.*
  - *As the maintainer, I can see from the capture report that the audio track
    is present and non-silent, so I do not have to audition the file to know
    the capture worked.*
- **Secondary — future CI / QA capture.** An eventual opt-in job that captures
  gameplay evidence benefits from clips that carry their own audio; the
  documented CI-cost impact is what the maintainer needs to decide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run capture` produces a WebM that contains a **game audio track**
   synchronised with the captured gameplay (the game's own SFX, not a
   separately generated bed), and the file remains playable video.
2. The audio track's presence is **verifiable without manual audition**: the
   in-page probe (or an equivalent automated check) confirms the recorded file
   has an audio track carrying a non-silent signal, and the capture report /
   `--json` payload records that result.
3. The audio-capture approach is described in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`,
   including **why it works under the browser autoplay policy** (the Enter
   gesture resumes the `AudioContext`) and how the audio is tapped from the
   game's single shared Web Audio graph.
4. Capture remains **opt-in and additive**: `npm test` and `npm run build` are
   unaffected, and the shipped Vite bundle is unchanged (`npm run
   check-bundle` still passes).
5. Any new tooling requirement (e.g. a full `ffmpeg` for external muxing, if
   that path is chosen) is documented in the known-limits / CI-cost sections,
   with the measured download/encode cost.
6. The pure capture helpers added by this change are covered by hermetic
   unit tests (no browser required), following the existing
   `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` pattern.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries
   (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`).
8. The full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Constraints

- **Opt-in only.** Capture tooling must stay outside the shipped bundle (no
  `src/` import from `scripts/`, or any `src/` addition gated behind a
  dev-only flag that `npm run check-bundle` accepts). Do **not** edit `.pi/`,
  `skill/`, or `command/` infrastructure.
- **Autoplay policy.** Browsers block `AudioContext` before a user gesture;
  audio only becomes capturable after the existing Enter keypress resumes the
  context.
- **Single shared context.** The game owns exactly one `AudioContext` (pinned
  to Phaser's sound manager by `installGameAudio`); capture must tap that
  graph rather than create a competing context.
- **Headless audio.** Headless Chromium is CPU-rendered and has no audio
  device; capture must rely on the Web Audio graph (a
  `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` renders regardless of hardware output),
  not on a system audio device.
- **No full `ffmpeg` on `PATH`.** Playwright's bundled ffmpeg is minimal (VP8
  only, no VP9/H.264), so any external mux is a new toolchain cost.
- **Output format** stays WebM (the spike's proven format); MP4 export remains
  out of scope.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` boots the game in headless Chromium, starts
  `PlayScene` with Enter, drives the deterministic bot, records
  `canvas.captureStream(60)` through `MediaRecorder` (VP9), probes the
  produced WebM in-page (resolution, duration, non-black fraction, colour
  variety, motion) and writes it to `capture-output/`.
- The probe (`isNonTrivialClip` in `scripts/capture-bot.mjs`) is pure and
  unit-tested; the browser/encode path is exercised only by `npm run capture`.
- Audio is a single shared `AudioContext` owned by
  `WebAudioSfxProvider` (`src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`), pinned to Phaser's
  context at boot by `installGameAudio` (`src/audio/effects.ts`, called from
  `MenuScene.create`). All SFX route through one master `GainNode`
  (`getMasterGain()`) connected to `context.destination`; the continuous
  thruster hum shares that master.
- `MenuScene`'s keyboard/pointer handlers call `resumeAudioContext(this.sound)`
  on the user gesture, and `installGameAudio` warms the baked-asset cache.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the current silent-clip limit and
  already sketches both candidate approaches.

## Desired change

Capture the game's Web Audio output during recording and include it as an
audio track in the WebM, defaulting to the in-page Web Audio approach:

- Route the shared SFX master output into a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`
  on the game's existing `AudioContext`, and combine its audio track with the
  canvas video track (`new MediaStream([...videoTracks, ...audioTracks])`)
  before handing the stream to `MediaRecorder`.
- Ensure the `AudioContext` is resumed by the existing Enter gesture before
  recording starts (document the autoplay-policy reasoning).
- Extend the in-page probe and report to assert the audio track exists and is
  non-silent, and surface the result in the human report and `--json` payload.
- Keep the offline WAV pipeline (`npm run build-audio`) out of the default
  path; document it (and any added `ffmpeg` requirement) as the rejected
  alternative in the known-limits / CI-cost sections.

### Candidate sub-approaches for tapping the audio graph

- **A1 (recommended) — page-side interception, no `src/` change.** Inject an
  init script (Playwright `addInitScript`) that wraps `AudioNode.prototype.connect`
  so any connection to the context's real `destination` is mirrored into a
  capture `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`. Keeps `src/` and the bundle
  untouched, satisfying the additive constraint most cheaply.
- **A2 — explicit dev-only hook.** Expose the master gain / an
  `enableAudioCapture()` seam from `src/audio/` behind a dev-only flag and call
  it from the capture script. More explicit and testable, but touches `src/`
  and must be excluded from the shipped bundle (`npm run check-bundle`).
- **B (rejected default) — offline WAV + external mux.** Reuse
  `scripts/build-audio.mjs` and mux the WAV with the captured WebM using a full
  `ffmpeg`. Not synchronised with in-game events and adds a heavy toolchain;
  retained only as a documented fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — add the audio tap, combine tracks, extend
  the probe and report (`--json` payload) with the audio result.
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` — extend the pure probe predicate / add audio
  helpers (kept pure and unit-tested).
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests for any new pure
  helpers (e.g. audio-track/verdict logic).
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` / `.d.mts` — report/formatting touch-ups if
  the audio result is rendered in the human report.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — replace the "Audio capture — deferred"
  known-limit with the implemented approach, autoplay rationale, verification
  and toolchain costs.
- `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`, `src/audio/effects.ts` — **only if A2** is
  chosen: a dev-only master-gain/capture seam (must not change the shipped
  bundle behaviour).
- `README.md` — pointer only if the command's behaviour/output description
  changes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — headless audio may be silent.** Headless Chromium may route Web
  Audio to a null backend, or the `AudioContext` may stay suspended if the
  Enter gesture is not honoured. *Mitigation:* rely on
  `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` (renders without hardware); add
  `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required` if the gesture resume proves
  flaky; verify non-silence in the probe rather than assuming it.
- **Risk — tuning the probe threshold.** AI_Hell audio is sparse at the start
  of level 1 (few enemies), so a low-peak clip is not necessarily a broken
  capture. *Mitigation:* assert "track present **and** non-silent above a
  small floor" and pick a warm-up window that includes shooting.
- **Risk — `MediaRecorder` audio codec.** The chosen WebM mime must include an
  audio codec (Opus) alongside VP9/VP8. *Mitigation:* select a mime type that
  `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported` confirms supports both; fall back and report.
- **Risk — A2 bundle leakage.** A dev-only `src/` hook could enter the shipped
  bundle. *Mitigation:* prefer A1; if A2, gate it so `npm run build` /
  `check-bundle` still pass.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** MP4 export, full `ffmpeg` install,
  audio-event synchronisation beyond "same recording", deterministic audio,
  and CI wiring are **out of scope**; record any such follow-up as a linked
  work item.
- **Assumption.** The audio to capture is the game's own SFX (the shared Web
  Audio graph), synchronised with gameplay; a separately generated bed is not
  acceptable for AC1.
- **Assumption.** WebM remains the output format; no MP4 requirement is added.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — the capture spike; delivers `npm run capture` and
  documents audio as explicitly deferred. This item is `discovered-from` it.
- **AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z** — the shared `AudioContext` / master-gain playback
  layer (`src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`, `src/audio/effects.ts`) this change taps.
- **AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD** — deterministic offline WAV build pipeline
  (`scripts/build-audio.mjs`); the rejected alternative's building block.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J** — ToneForge audio migration (single-context
  guarantee) that makes a single tap point possible.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A** – Dedicated player-destruction SFX (completed)
- **AH-0MUNX32FA006RY4T** – [test-failure] src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — boss encounter (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) > AC1 — the Central AI spawns after Level 5 is cleared, with Phase-1 minions — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3** – Add an extra life power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muwmff3c002wobk, acceptance, added, additive, alternative (+92 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: 0muwmff3c002wobk, added, additive, alternative, approach (+77 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: added, additive, alternative, approach, approaches (+71 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (intake agent, to self / repo search): Is the seed context sufficient to
  draft a clear brief without an interview round?**
  — **Answer:** Yes. The seed already supplies the problem, user story,
  candidate approaches and six measurable acceptance criteria, and the
  `discovered-from` spike and its implementation comment supply the existing
  state. Repo inspection confirmed the audio architecture
  (`src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`, `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`),
  the capture pipeline (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`) and the documented
  deferred-audio limit (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`). No clarifying
  questions required. Source: seed description + repo inspection.
- **Q (intake agent, to self): Which approach should be committed to?**
  — **Answer (recommendation, advisory):** Approach A (live in-page Web Audio
  capture) over approach B (offline WAV + `ffmpeg` mux), because AC1 requires
  audio synchronised with the captured gameplay and A adds no heavy toolchain.
  Within A, prefer A1 (page-side `connect` interception) over A2 (dev-only
  `src/` hook) to keep `src/` and the shipped bundle untouched. Source: seed
  description candidate approaches + repo inspection. This is a recommendation;
  planning may revisit it.
- **Q (intake agent, to self): How is audio presence verified?**
  — **Answer:** Via the in-page probe — assert the combined stream has a live
  audio track, then check the recorded blob's audio is non-silent (e.g.
  `AudioContext.decodeAudioData` peak/RMS, or `webkitAudioDecodedByteCount`),
  and record the result in the report and `--json` payload (AC2/AC3). Source:
  seed AC3 + repo inspection of the existing probe.

---

## Plan (plan skill)

Decomposed into four child items — dependency-ordered and test-first. F1 lands
the pure, hermetic verification logic first; F2 is the end-to-end capture
slice (prototype-gated because headless audio is the principal unknown); F3
adds the observability/verification layer; F4 documents the shipped behaviour.

| # | Child item | Type | Depends on |
|---|-----------|------|-----------|
| F1 | Pure audio/mime helpers with hermetic tests (AH-0MUWYQQMZ007QIQZ) | task | — |
| F2 | Tap shared Web Audio into the recording (AH-0MUWYQQYU001G6OG) | feature | F1 |
| F3 | Verify non-silent audio in probe and report (AH-0MUWYQRAS0054VO5) | feature | F2 |
| F4 | Document audio capture and costs (AH-0MUWYQRML000FLMT) | docs | F3 |

**Vertical slices.** F1 = pure helpers + tests (the contract). F2 = tap →
track mux → recorded WebM (end-to-end, prototype gate on headless
non-silence). F3 = decode/measure → report/`--json` → exit-code (end-to-end
observability). F4 = docs. Between phases the next item's description is
reviewed and updated against what F(n-1) actually delivered.

**Decision: approach A1** (page-side `AudioNode.prototype.connect`
interception) over A2 (dev-only `src/` hook), because A1 keeps `src/` and the
shipped bundle untouched. A2 is retained as the documented fallback if the F2
feasibility gate fails.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-06T17:39:43Z — plan skill: initial decomposition into 4 children; wired deps
  F2←F1, F3←F2, F4←F3; appended this plan and the planning Appendix. Coverage
  review: `proceed`.

### Appendix: planning Q&A

- **Q (plan agent): Which audio-tap approach is committed?**
  — **Answer (plan agent, advisory):** A1 — page-side
  `AudioNode.prototype.connect` interception — because it leaves `src/` and
  the shipped Vite bundle untouched; A2 (dev-only `src/` seam) is retained
  only as the documented fallback if the F2 feasibility gate fails.
  Source: seed "Candidate sub-approaches" + F2 prototype AC6.
- **Q (plan agent): Should a missing/silent audio track fail the capture?**
  — **Answer (plan agent, advisory):** Yes — treat it like the existing video
  verdict: a reason and a non-zero exit, so `npm run capture` cannot silently
  emit a silent clip; if headless audio proves infeasible the measured finding
  and fallback are recorded instead.
  Source: seed AC1/AC2 + F3 AC2.
- **Q (plan agent): Which WebM mime should be selected?**
  — **Answer (plan agent, advisory):** prefer `video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus`,
  then `video/webm;codecs=vp8,opus`, then plain `video/webm`, chosen through
  `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported`.
  Source: seed risk "MediaRecorder audio codec" + F1 AC1.
- **Q (plan agent): Are all parent acceptance criteria collectively covered?**
  — **Answer (plan agent):** Yes — F1/F2/F3 cover AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6 and AC8;
  F4 covers AC3, AC5 and AC7. The `tree_coverage` helper reports `proceed`
  (note: its AC extractor recognises only `- ` bullets, while this project's
  ACs are numbered, so the coverage count is advisory rather than exhaustive).
  Source: `tree_coverage.py run-coverage-review AH-0MUWTNPYJ0031FQE`.

**OPEN QUESTIONS:** none.

## Goal

Document the implemented audio-capture approach — the autoplay rationale, the
shared Web Audio tap point, how non-silence is verified, and any added
toolchain/CI cost — replacing the deferred-audio known limit
(AH-0MUWTNPYJ0031FQE, AC3/AC5/AC7).

**User story:** As a future maintainer (or CI owner), I can read one document
and understand how capture gets audio, why it works in a browser under the
autoplay policy, how it is verified, and what it costs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` replaces the "Audio capture — explicitly
   deferred" section with the implemented A1 approach: the page-side
   `AudioNode.prototype.connect` interception, the single shared
   `AudioContext` / master-gain tap point, and the exact WebM/Opus mime used.
2. It explains why it works under the browser autoplay policy (the Enter
   keypress resumes the `AudioContext`) and that the
   `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` renders without any system audio device.
3. The known-limits / CI-cost sections record the measured encode/CPU impact of
   adding audio, and explicitly retain the rejected offline-WAV + `ffmpeg` mux
   alternative, noting no full `ffmpeg` is required for the shipped path.
4. `README.md`'s automated-capture bullet no longer says audio is deferred and
   notes that the report includes the audio result.
5. All documentation assertions in `npm test` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Rewrite the deferred-audio subsection into "Audio capture" (approach, tap
  point, mime) + "Autoplay policy" + "Audio verification" sub-parts.
- Update the pipeline numbered list to include the audio tap/mux step.
- Update the file table and CI-cost bullets; keep edits to `README.md` to the
